client_alerts.headline: Xen XSA-523: guest-to-guest memory access (found by Claude)
client_alerts.body: Xen advisory XSA-523 (Nov 3) covers two grant-copy flaws (CVE-2026-102703/102704) that could let a malicious guest read other VMs' memory, affecting **Xen 4.6 and later**. Any client running Xen-based hypervisors (XCP-ng, Citrix Hypervisor, some hosting/DR providers) should confirm their patch timeline and ask recovery-site vendors the same question.

client_alerts.headline: "Prompt adware" injected into OpenAI Codex configuration
client_alerts.body: Check Point described a jailbreak bundle that plants ads in Codex's configuration files. Clients letting developers use coding agents should treat agent config files as code: review them, pin them in source control, and scan them, since a tampered config travels with every session.

top_moves.title: Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and Microsoft back one robots.txt signal for AI-training opt-out
top_moves.body: A shared `__usage_ai-training` token, submitted to the IETF by Anthropic, lets a site opt out of training for all participating crawlers at once. Microsoft honors it from **Feb 1, 2027**, Google in early 2027, and Meta has not committed. It does not remove anything already collected.

top_moves.title: Claude credited with Xen hypervisor flaws that break VM isolation
top_moves.body: XSA-523 fixes two grant-copy bugs Claude found, which could let one guest read another VM's memory on Xen 4.6+. It is a direct patching item for virtualized DR sites, and further evidence that AI-driven vulnerability discovery is speeding up patch cadence.

top_moves.title: Voters reject data-center expansion in 40 of 41 local measures; OpenAI responds with a Community Compact
top_moves.body: Local voters, including in at least 14 Ohio municipalities, voted down or restricted data centers. OpenAI pledged to drop NDAs with officials and cover full power costs at its own sites. AI capacity is now constrained by politics as well as chips, which matters for region and capacity assumptions in DR plans.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: National Community Compact for data centers; Brockman says Q3 revenue turned around and business customers are now the majority.
providers.detail: OpenAI published a National Community Compact (no NDAs with public officials, full power and infrastructure costs covered at owned sites, $80M named for Effingham County, GA) after local ballot measures went heavily against data centers. Greg Brockman told WSJ Tech Live that annualized revenue rose about 70% in Q3, with business customers now more than half of revenue. Separately, Check Point reported "prompt adware" planted in Codex configuration. No new ChatGPT model or feature release surfaced.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Amended S-1 lists $17.0B Q3 revenue and ~$895B in compute commitments; Claude found the XSA-523 Xen flaws.
providers.detail: The Nov 2 S-1 amendment reports $17.0B in Jul–Sep sales and about $895.4B in signed compute and infrastructure contracts; Nov 10 is the earliest possible roadshow date. Google will credit-backstop roughly $19B of Anthropic's lease obligations at a 401MW Kentucky campus. Claude is credited with two Xen vulnerabilities (XSA-523). A judge dismissed the direct copyright claim against Dario Amodei in the Concord Music case, with leave to amend.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: EU advocate general says Gemini may infringe publisher rights; Google backstops a $19B Anthropic lease.
providers.detail: An EU Court of Justice advocate general's opinion said Gemini could infringe publisher rights through paywall circumvention and reproduction of article text. The opinion is not a ruling, but it signals legal exposure for EU deployments. Google also joined the shared AI-training opt-out signal, with support planned for early 2027. No new model shipped in the last 48 hours.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Quiet. Grok 5 still unshipped past the Oct 31 date it had been expected by.
providers.detail: No new release surfaced. Grok 4.7 (GitHub Copilot, Sep 21) remains the latest model in coding tools.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: Quiet. Supports a common AI-training standard but hasn't committed to honoring the new token.
providers.detail: No Llama or Muse release. Meta is the one major crawler operator that has not confirmed it will honor the shared `__usage_ai-training` opt-out.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: Quiet after Large 4 open weights. No new ship.
providers.detail: No new release in the window. Large 4 (1T parameters, open weights) remains the on-prem option to evaluate for data-residency-sensitive clients.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: Quiet. No new feature or policy change found.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: Will honor the AI-training opt-out from Feb 1, 2027; reportedly declined to expand its Nscale Texas contract.
providers.detail: Microsoft treats training and grounding (what feeds Copilot answers) as separate controls under the new signal, starting Feb 1, 2027. The FT reports Microsoft declined an option to more than double its Nscale Texas data-center contract. No new Copilot feature shipped.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: No new ship found.
providers.detail: No November changelog items surfaced in search.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: No new ship found.
providers.detail: No Cursor news in the window. Competitor Cognition released SWE-2 Flash, a faster, cheaper coding model.
